title: Homework · A Postcard From a New Home

overview.title: A Postcard From a New Home
overview.goal: Recall target expressions and write a friendly 80–100-word postcard from a fictional new home.

steps.title: 01 · A quick memory check
steps.instruction: Match these phrases to their meanings. Try without opening the lesson.
source: Vocabulary from Would You Live Here?: settle in, feel at home, get used to, make friends, miss home, give it a try.
Check your answers, then write ONE sentence aloud using two of the expressions.
items: get comfortable in a new place
Feel at home is about comfort, not owning a property.
A new routine can help you make friends.
wish you were with familiar people or places
Give it a try = test the experience.
steps.teacherNotes: 5 min, optional quick oral follow-up. Old homework responses retained under their previous step IDs and the same protected progress key.

steps.title: 02 · A postcard from a new home
steps.instruction: Imagine someone has spent one month living in another country. Write a friendly postcard to a friend (80–100 words). It can be fictional.
source: Your postcard should include: ① where you live; ② what your normal weekday looks like; ③ one new thing you have got used to; ④ something you miss; ⑤ whether you want to stay longer and why.
Use at least THREE expressions from this lesson: settle in / feel at home / get used to / make friends / miss home / give it a try.
Start naturally: 'Hi Alex! I've been in Porto for a month now. At first ...'. Finish with a friendly question for your friend.
Check: 80–100 words, at least three expressions, used to / get used to correctly, and a clear ending.
steps.teacherNotes: 15 min. Mark for meaning, clarity and three target phrases. This is the separately published homework without video call.
